key_insight: The paper rigorously proves that topological quantum codes can still exhibit a positive error threshold under coherent Z-rotation noise, with logical infidelity decaying exponentially with code distance below a size-independent angle limit.
engineering_relevance: This strengthens the theoretical case for using surface code and related topological LDPC codes in hardware where control errors are coherent rather than purely stochastic.
method: Uses Fourier analysis to preserve interference between coherent error amplitudes.
Applies cluster expansion of abstract polymer models to bound logical failure.
Analyzes maximum-likelihood Pauli recovery for bounded-logical-qubit topological codes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a rigorous threshold proof and an exponential suppression guarantee for entanglement infidelity under coherent rotation angles below a constant independent of code size.
watch_item: The result is proven for coherent Z-rotation errors and codes with a bounded number of logical qubits, so broader noise models and finite-precision decoder implementations may need separate validation.
paper_title: Proof of a positive coherent-error threshold for topological quantum codes
